subject: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal

Aaron —

Thanks again for the time this week. Attached is the updated order form (v3) and a one-page SLA tier mapping that aligns Helix’s internal service tiers with Redwood’s service levels for the upcoming renewal. The two short items we need to close before we send to your legal team:

1) Exhibit E pricing bands — we moved Helix from Tier 2 -> Tier 3 for the expanded usage profile (as discussed). Please confirm that aligns with your internal forecasting.
2) Incident response SLA hours — Redwood proposes the 4-hour P1 response stay in place, with a 12-month credit cap for repeated breaches (language in redlines_annotated.docx).

Requested next steps: could you confirm receipt and provide the appropriate contracts contact (if different from procurement@helixanalytics.com)? If the procurement team is comfortable, we can push the annotated doc to legal for redlines; otherwise, let me know any immediate dealbreakers.

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_Helix_v3.xlsx; SLA-Tier-Mapping_Helix_vs_Redwood.pdf; redlines_annotated.docx

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@helixanalytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@helixanalytics.com>, contracts@helixanalytics.com
Date: 2028-08-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal

Naomi —

Thanks for sending. Quick responses inline:

- Pricing band move to Tier 3: Okay from a spend perspective, but I need to confirm with finance we can absorb the uplift for Q4. I should know by end of day Friday (2028-08-04).
- P1 SLA + 12-month credit cap: Procurement flagged the credit cap wording — they prefer a per-incident credit with a quarterly aggregate cap rather than a 12-month rolling cap. Can you share a short rationale for the 12-month language?

Also, contracts@helixanalytics.com is the right place to send the annotated doc for legal review. I'll introduce a signing contact once we have legal's redline set.

For context, procurement also asked whether Redwood can accept a short off-ramp for overage usage that includes a 30-day notice and prorated true-up. Is that already reflected somewhere?

Appreciate the speed here — we’re trying to keep this on the same cadence as our product launch.

Best,
Aaron
Director, Strategic Procurement
Helix Analytics
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal

Aaron — thanks for the quick review and the flags. Answers below and attaching a short note for legal to consider.

1) 12-month credit cap rationale: the intent is to limit cumulative exposure for recurring incidents tied to the same root cause. From an ops standpoint, a 12-month window maps to our incident triage and remediation cycles and keeps credits predictable for both parties. If procurement prefers a quarterly cap, we can propose: per-incident credit + quarterly aggregate cap equal to 20% of monthly invoice (examples in redlines_annotated.docx, pg2).

2) Off-ramp / overage: we can accept a 30-day notice + prorated true-up with a small administrative fee (0.5% of the monthly invoice) for mid-term terminations triggered by overage. I've put suggested language in the order form (see tab 'Offramp' in v3).

Next suggested flow:
- I'll share redlines_annotated.docx with contracts@helixanalytics.com and request their markups.
- Marissa (legal ops) and Karthik (senior counsel) are on copy to expedite legal Q&A.

If finance confirms Tier 3 by Friday, we'll target legal redlines by next Tuesday so we can get this into signatures before your launch window.

Thanks —
Naomi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: contracts@helixanalytics.com <contracts@helixanalytics.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aaron Li <aaron.li@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-03T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal — Redwood proposed edits

Hi Aaron / Helix contracts team —

Thanks for the questions — I pulled together a short memo and added inline suggestions to redlines_annotated.docx. A few highlights:

- Credit window: we can accept a quarterly aggregate cap instead of a 12-month rolling cap, provided Helix accepts a modest per-incident credit floor and commits to the remediation timeline in Section 4.2. Our suggested text is highlighted in the doc.
- Off-ramp language: we pushed the 0.5% admin fee down to 0.25% to make the off-ramp less punitive. We proposed a 60-day notice for operational continuity (see orderform v3 tab 'Offramp').
- Exhibit E pricing: we clarified that the Tier 3 rates apply once monthly usage exceeds 1.2x the committed units for two consecutive months. This prevents sudden step-ups on single-month spikes.

We tried to balance predictability for Helix with guardrails for Redwood. We're happy to jump on a short call to finalize language. If Helix can provide initial redlines by EOD Monday (2028-08-06), we can respond quickly and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Attachments: redlines_annotated.docx (inlined comments), SLA-Tier-Mapping_Helix_vs_Redwood.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@helixanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@helixanalytics.com <contracts@helixanalytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@helixanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-04T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA tier mapping + order form alignment for renewal — next steps

Marissa / Naomi —

Appreciate the thoroughness. Quick update from our side: finance approved the Tier 3 move contingent on the quarterly guardrails you proposed. Contracts has reviewed your annotated doc and uploaded Helix_marked_redlines.docx to the shared link (contracts@helixanalytics.com). Key asks from legal:

- Change ‘12-month rolling’ language to ‘quarterly aggregate cap’ as suggested (good to confirm exact percentage in doc).
- Keep the 30-day off-ramp but remove administrative fee — procurement says Helix's procurement policy prohibits mid-term commercial penalties for overage-driven off-ramps.

We can accept the Exhibit E definition that applies after two consecutive months >1.2x committed units.

Next steps per our timeline:
- Helix legal will send the marked redlines by EOD tomorrow (2028-08-05).
- Assuming alignment, we can do DocuSign by 2028-08-09 and aim for the renewal to be effective 2028-09-01.

Thanks all — Naomi, please let me know if Redwood can remove the admin fee in the offramp clause; if not, flag for escalation and we’ll find a middle path.

Best,
Aaron
